Fig. 3.2. The classical GA is a directed graph with two loops. The initial population of Npop genotypes (on the right) give rise to phenotypes, which are in turn used to evaluate the fitnesses of the Npop individuals in the “environment”, which are then collected as a ranked population of parent genotypes (on the left). The fitness ranking of an individual determines the probability of it being selected to take part in a breeding pair. Npop/2 breeding pairs are formed in this manner, and then crossover and mutation yield an entirely new generation, and the process is repeated.

Linear couplings are coloured from dark blue (large negative terms) to dark red (large positive terms).
